title: Trust bridge scratch — SOC2 prep flow and loose mapping
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for mapping likely SOC2 evidence and questions we still need to triage. This is messy on purpose — notes to self + things to hand off to Samir/Maya when they have bandwidth.

Top-level goals (short):
- Identify minimal evidence set for Security (TSC: Security) and Availability that can scale across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Draft sampling approach for access reviews / change management (what population, cadence).
- Capture weird edge-cases for Private deployments (air-gapped evidence, on-prem KMS).

Open questions (urgent):
1) Access review population: do we sample by role or by org unit? For small infra groups role-based seems easier. Need to confirm with HR data export availability (CSV from People ops).
2) How do we show automated log retention for private deployments where logs are customer-managed? Proposed: provide docs + test instance with agent enabled + signed customer attestation?
3) For model rollout change control: what counts as a change? Full model weight update vs config/quantization tweak? Recommend: treat model version bump as change, optimization params (batch size/quant) as operational tuning (documented).

Quick control -> evidence sketches (one-liners):
- User access provisioning: evidence = onboarding checklist + joiner/leaver report (CSV) + sample access review emails. Owner: People Ops + SRE. JIRA link: JIRA-SEC-314
- Privileged access (ops keys): evidence = key rotation logs (KMS rotation events) + runbook for emergency access. Owner: infra.
- Logging & monitoring: evidence = ELK/obs dashboards screenshots + retention policy doc + alert runbooks. For Private: config template + customer guidance doc.
- Change management (model/deploy): evidence = PR audit trail (GitHub PRs, approvals), CI/CD pipeline history, deploy runbook.
- Incident response: evidence = 1-2 redacted incident reports + tabletop notes + postmortem template used.
- Vendor mgmt (cloud infra): evidence = contracts, risk assessment spreadsheet, SOC2 of vendor (if available).

Sampling / testing plan (sketch):
- Access reviews: sample 10% of active accounts OR min 5 accounts per critical role, whichever larger. Period = last 12 months.
- Deploy changes: sample 6 deploys across months (mix small/large). Look for approvals and rollback docs.
- Log retention: check 3 random log streams (auth, deploy, infra-alert) for retention metadata and raw events.

Evidence collection TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Export People ops user CSV and map roles -> send to Samir (deadline 2026-03-10).
- [ ] Pull last 12 months of KMS rotation events (infra) + anonymize -> attach.
- [ ] Draft small template: "Evidence packet — Hosted vs Private" with required items and acceptable alternate artifacts. Use that as checklist for solutions engineering handoff.

Notes & fudge factors:
- Private deployments: we cannot always provide centralized logs or KMS events. Need to decide acceptable alternates early (customer-controlled evidence + signed attestation).
- Automation: try to script evidence pulls for core items to avoid manual hunting later. Minimal viable script: People CSV export, KMS list, GH PR list, SSO audit.

Rough timeline thoughts:
- Week 0–2: baseline docs + evidence template + sample exports
- Week 3–4: collect samples and anonymize -> produce 3 evidence packets
- Week 5: internal dry run with auditors (pilot)

Random scribbles / heuristics:
- If a control relies on human judgment (e.g., code review quality), capture 3 examples with reviewer comments rather than a generic statement.
- When in doubt, include a short annotated screenshot — auditors like concrete traces.

Hand-off notes: when I pass this to Samir/Maya: prioritize People CSV + KMS rotation + 3 PRs. I'll draft the evidence packet template and drop in Confluence/this slack channel for visibility.

End of scratchpad. Will clean into formal checklist after team sync.
summary: Personal scratch notes for SOC2 evidence mapping and sampling; informal, actionable TODOs and open questions for trust-ops.
